      "rationale": "Emphasis/shouting is a plausible stylistic predictor of strong (often negative) affect. Values are mechanically derivable from text and samples look consistent, though acronyms like 'DVD' may inflate counts."
    },
    {
      "name": "exclamation_mark_count",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.6,
      "source_groundedness": 0.95,

      "analytical_usefulness": 0.55,
      "source_groundedness": 0.95,
      "hallucination_observed": false,

      "source_groundedness": 0.9,

      "analytical_usefulness": 0.35,
      "source_groundedness": 1.0,

      "analytical_usefulness": 0.4,

    {

      "analytical_usefulness": 0.65,
      "source_groundedness": 0.8,
      "hallucination_observed": false,

  "analytical_usefulness": 0.62,
  "source_groundedness": 0.83,
  "rationale": "Most columns provide genuine, distinct axes (sentiment counts, emphasis/punctuation intensity, complaint-topic detectors) directly relevant to predicting negative satisfaction. A few (title_word_count, content_word_count) are generic length features with weak leverage. Values are largely mechanically or lexically derivable from the source text with no invented facts; groundedness is dented only by imperfect lexicons that mis-detect polarity (e.g., investment_complaint firing on a positive price mention, sentiment lexicons missing clearly affective rows). No confident fabrication observed."
